117592.name: Lubavitch Hebrew Academy
117592.note: COLlive, 4 Sept 2024: Rabbi Yossie Denburg, 'the founder and dean of LHA': 'As we begin our 40th year of service ... the Rebbe's Bracha to my wife and I in 5745, for Hatzlacha for Chinuch in Broward County' (a 40th year in 2024-25 gives a first year of 1985-86). School listings: founded in 1985. (Earlier called the Hebrew Academy Community School.)

117597.name: Chabad of Greater Orlando
117597.note: Heritage Florida Jewish News (COLlive, 1 Jan 2010): 'This year, Chabad of Greater Orlando will celebrate 25 years of service in Orlando. Since its inception in 1985'; the Dubovs 'were chosen as ambassadors ... shortly after they wed in September 1984'. Heritage (2019): established in 1985. Its own site says 'founded in 1984' (the year of the appointment). Began in a small storefront.

118287.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Sunny Isles Beach
118287.note: Its CYP page: 'Our synagogue began as Sunny Isles Chabad in 1994 even before Sunny Isles Beach was incorporated or named as a city', in 'a small office space on the second floor of the RK Plaza at 170th Street'; 'Various moves followed until eventually, the congregation moved to the ground floor of the King David in 2004.' Confirmed by the IRS record: 'Chabad Center Of Sunny Isles Inc', exempt from Aug 1994 (ProPublica). Rabbi Yisrael and Toby Baron.

earlier.where: an office on the second floor of RK Plaza, 170th Street
the ground floor of the King David

117960.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Southwest Broward
117960.note: COLlive, 18 July 2022: 'After a unique and life changing blessing from the Rebbe 31 years ago, Rabbi Pinny and Gitty moved to Florida to be trailblazing shluchim, opening Chabad of Southwest Broward (SWB) in Cooper City', 'operating out of a small modest modular trailer for 30 years' (so 1992). IRS: 'Chabad Lubavitch Of Southwest Broward Inc', exempt from Dec 1993 (ProPublica). therebbesimpact.com: the couple 1992, the center 1993.

earlier.where: a small modular trailer, Cooper City

118284.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Martin & S. Lucie County
118284.note: 10 Sept 2018: Rabbi Shlomo and Daniella Uminer's Chabad center, 'which they founded when they moved here from Brooklyn 23 years ago' (so 1995); Lubavitch.com, separately: they have led the community for 23 years. IRS: 'Chabad Jewish Center Of Martin-St Lucie County Inc', exempt from Feb 2001. (therebbesimpact.com: 1999.) A 2.5-acre campus on Sunset Trail, Palm City.

118411.name: Chabad Key Biscayne Jewish Center
118411.note: Lubavitch.com, 11 Nov 2002: 'three years ago, Rabbi Yoel and Rivka Caroline began introducing various Jewish activities' on Key Biscayne (so 1999); Chabad of Key Biscayne 'moved into a home of its own just in time Rosh Hashana 5763' (Sept 2002) at 211 Greenwood Drive. IRS: 'Chabad Of Key Biscayne Inc', exempt from May 2002. Now 101 Harbor Drive (Rabbi Avremel Caroline).

118437.name: Chabad of South Orlando
118437.note: Heritage Florida Jewish News, 3 Apr 2015: 'After having a presence in the southwest Orlando area for 15 years' (so 2000); Chabad.org, separately: 'the 2000 arrival of Rabbi Yosef and Chani Konikov'. (Chabad of Greater Orlando's history has them hired in 1998; a 2016 Heritage piece says 1999; an Anash account says activities began in 2001 from their rented home.) Earlier on Tamarind Circle; the Center of Jewish Life at 7347 Sand Lake Road from about 2015.

earlier.where: Orlando: Universal Boulevard (its location in 2014, before the move to Sand Lake Road)

118475.name: Chabad of Coral Springs
118475.note: Anash ('Chabad of Coral Springs celebrates 36 years and counting'): 'Established in 1986, Chabad of Coral Springs began when Rabbi Yossi Denburg and his wife Rivka were sent to South Florida' to build a Hebrew day school and a Chabad House; Rabbi Avraham Friedman became executive director in 1991. (Coral Springs Talk counted its 36th anniversary in 2023, and therebbesimpact.com says 1987: a year later.)

118658.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Jupiter
118658.note: TCPalm (via CrownHeights.info, 1 April 2006): 'The three-year-old orthodox synagogue has closed on 1.5 acres at University Boulevard' (so 2003), said founder Rabbi Berel Barash. IRS: 'Chabad Jewish Center Of Jupiter Inc', care of Dov Ber Barash, exempt from Dec 2004. Its two-story center at 430 University Blvd. was due late 2018.

118660.name: California Club Chabad
118660.note: Rabbi Shloime and Feigie Halsband's own page: 'The California Club Chabad opened its doors in 2003'; it began in a mall and 'after two years we purchased a house to serve as our shul' (825 NE 205 Terrace). (A tribute calls the late Rabbi Dovid Bryn, d. 2002, founder of 'the California Club Shul' too: an earlier minyan there, perhaps.)

212291.name: Chabad of Bonita Springs, Estero & FGCU
212291.note: The Banner (via CrownHeights.info, 25 May 2007): building a synagogue 'is a dream for the 3-year-old Chabad of Bonita Springs and Estero' (Rabbi Mendy Greenberg); Naples News (CrownHeights.info, 10 Sept 2007): 'Greenberg and his wife started services out of their home three years ago. We've accomplished a lot in the short three years since we've opened' (both: 2004). IRS: 'Chabad Of Bonita Springs Inc', exempt from April 2005.

earlier.where: an office suite in a strip mall off Old 41 Road (Bernwood Centre), Bonita Springs

334256.name: Chabad of Southside
334256.note: CrownHeights.info, 4 Sept 2007: 'Just a short year after first opening its doors, Chabad of Southside in Jacksonville, Florida welcomed a brand new Torah'; Patch (Jacksonville), on the Finker-Frenkel Chabad Center: it 'has serviced the area's hundreds of college students and the larger Jacksonville community since opening its doors in 2006'. Rabbi Shmuel (Shmuli) and Chana Novack; early on in rented meeting rooms and libraries; the 12,000 sq ft center opened in 2019.

earlier.where: Jacksonville: a small facility near UNF, outgrown by 2016 (a $2.4 million building was then planned)

347029.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Doral
347029.note: Miami Herald (CrownHeights.info, 16 Oct 2006, at Sukkot): 'Since their arrival in Doral a year ago, the Brashevitzky family has welcomed ... worshipers for weekly Chabad services held at their home, 5353 NW 109th Ct.'; 'One year ago, he established the Chabad Jewish Center in Doral' (fall 2005). IRS: 'Chabad Jewish Center Of Doral Inc', exempt from June 2006. (Later counts are a year short: Miami Herald, May 2009, 'three years later'; Doral Family Journal, 23 March 2013, 'established seven years ago'.) Then a two-floor space in a shopping center at 9725 NW 41st St.; now 10181 NW 58th St.

927742.name: French Chabad of Florida
927742.note: Lubavitch.com, 11 June 2007: 'Sixteen years ago upon arriving in Miami, Rabbi Frankforter advertised Torah classes for French speakers' (so 1991); COLlive, separately: Rabbi Yisroel and Louiza Frankforter 'have been servicing the French community of South Florida and the many French-speaking tourists who visit since 1991'. Registered later as the Jewish Educational Leadership Institute (IRS ruling 2005).

589520.name: Chabad of Royal Palm Beach
589520.note: Town-Crier (22 Nov 2013): 'Chabad of Royal Palm Beach has been in existence for about six years' (count back: 2007); Rabbi Nachman Zeev (Zevi) Schtroks: 'We got married in Israel ... After spending a few months in Israel, we went to New York, and within about three months, we came to Florida'; their own page: 'In the summer of 2006, Rabbi Zevi and Leah got married in Israel' (so they came about early 2007). He came at the suggestion of his uncle Rabbi Mendy Muskal (Wellington); it started with monthly lunch-and-learns, ran from an office at 11440 Okeechobee Blvd. for several years, and in 2013 took over the former Temple Beth Zion, 129 Sparrow Drive.

118013.name: Chabad Center of Kendall & Pinecrest
118013.note: Rabbi Yossi Harlig (VoyageMIA interview): 'When I and my wife Nechama arrived in Kendall in 1995, we carried little more than a vision'; 'Nearly three decades after opening our living room to the community'; the center later rose on property at SW 87th Avenue and SW 112th Street. IRS: 'Chabad Center Of Kendall Inc', exempt from March 1998. therebbesimpact.com: 1995.

4544860.name: Chabad at the City of Delray Beach
4544860.note: COLlive, 18 Dec 2019: 'Rabbi Mendy and Mirel Heber, together with their daughter Rochel Leah, are the new Shluchim to Delray Beach, Florida' (delrayjewish.com). IRS: 'Chabad At The City Of Delray Beach Inc', exempt from Aug 2020.

4364240.name: Chabad of Bayshore, Miami Beach
4364240.note: COLlive, 18 June 2019: 'Rabbi Shmuli and Sara Basya Lezak ... will be moving in the coming weeks to the neighborhood of Bayshore in Miami Beach, Florida. The Lezaks will be establishing a Chabad center there'; appointed by Rabbi Avrohom Korf. IRS: 'Chabad Of Bayshore', exempt from May 2021.

5151499.name: Camp Gan Izzy
5151499.note: Camp Gan Izzy of Rabbi Mendy and Mirel Heber, who became the shluchim to Delray Beach in Dec 2019 (COLlive): so it began after 2019. Its own start year not found yet; lead: the chabad.org listing is from about 2021.
